report.source_text: Clinical examination revealed bilateral conjunctival inflammation and three blister-type skin lesions on the arms and legs. Inspection of the oral cavity showed mucosal ulcerations of the ventral tongue (figure 1), cheeks, soft palate (figure 2), uvula and posterior oropharyngeal wall. A flexible transnasal endoscopy revealed crusts on the right middle turbinate and nasopharynx, as well as diffuse whitish pseudomembrane-covered erosions of almost all the supraglottic area and posterior hypopharyngeal wall (figure 3).

clinician.final_diagnosis: Mucous membrane pemphigoid (MMP) with diffuse oral, ocular, nasal, cutaneous, pharyngeal and laryngeal involvement
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 73-year-old woman presented with diffuse oral burning, disabling pharyngodynia, weight loss, cough, hoarseness, dyspnoea, ocular irritation, and nail inflammation. Physical exam revealed multisite involvement including bilateral conjunctival inflammation, oral mucosal ulcerations, nasal crusts, blister-type skin lesions, and supraglottic and pharyngeal erosions. Previous oral biopsies showed fibrin deposits without malignancy. Direct immunofluorescence demonstrated linear IgG and C3 deposits at the dermo-epidermal junction, confirming immunopathological involvement. Serology revealed circulating anti-BP180 autoantibodies (26.99 U/mL), negative for BP230, supporting MMP. PET-CT showed left supraclavicular and retroperitoneal adenopathies, but biopsy results of lymphadenopathy remain unavailable. Despite absence of biopsy confirmation of lymphadenopathies and treatment/outcome data, the clinical, histological, and serological evidence firmly supports the diagnosis of MMP with multisite mucosal and cutaneous involvement.
